name: VAG DQ250 / 02E 6-speed DSG TCU (Temic, TriCore generation)
notes: Later 02E (DQ250, PQ35/PQ46) software built for a little-endian Infineon TriCore (the code decodes as TriCore; e.g. 02E300013N, Golf VI GTI / R). Read as 0xB0000 bytes: a 64 KiB calibration block at 0x0-0xFFFF (ident record '<nn>02E300013N  GSG DSG AG6 ... DCT' near 0x3668, version tag 'v0697...__getriebe_DSG_...' at 0xFFC0) followed by the code from 0x10000. No checksum is claimed: neither the 02E CRC-16 sector table nor the DQ250-MQB JAMCRC holds on the available reads, so checksum is null and edited images cannot be corrected. Diagnostics as for temic-dq250-02e (transport/layer unconfirmed; set to match the car); no OBD full-read path is documented. Maps: the two shift-speed schedule groups, located by structure only (raw, MEDIUM). Calibration only.

maps.name: shift schedule 1 - upshift 1-2 (inferred)
maps.notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM (location/shape HIGH, role and unit inferred). Source: OpenTune's own analysis of two real 02E300013N reads (no A2L/XDF/commercial map pack): the same 4x12 block structure and row shape as the shift schedules of the PowerPC-generation 02E software, located by structure only (the two available datasets of this software do not differ inside these blocks). 4 rows x 12 columns of u16 little-endian. Every row rises monotonically from a flat low plateau to a flat high plateau and the values sit in the engine-speed band of the drivetrain the calibration was built for, which is the shape of a DSG shift-speed schedule; this is block 1 of 5 consecutive 0x60-byte upshift blocks, inferred to be the 1-2 upshift. Set 1 is the first of two groups; which driving programme each group serves is not established. Axes (12 columns - likely accelerator pedal - and 4 rows) are not located, so cells ship raw; edit by ratio. Addresses are offsets into the 0xB0000-byte 02E300013N read (64 KiB CAL first, then code); other TriCore 02E software may differ - confirm by content in your own read before any write. No checksum is known for this layout, so a written image cannot be corrected by OpenTune.
